references.text: God had already warned Balak that Bileam could not curse Israel because the people were blessed.
Bileam acknowledges that he cannot curse those whom God has not cursed, which explains Balak's frustration.
Balak's earlier complaint that Bileam blessed instead of cursing, reflecting the same frustration.
Bileam explains that he has received a command to bless and cannot change it.
Balak's anger when Bileam blesses Israel for the third time, continuing the conflict described here.
God's promise to Abraham to bless those who bless his descendants and curse those who curse them, the basis for Israel's protection.
Isaac's blessing over Jacob includes a curse on those who curse him, the same principle that protects Israel.
